stories.title: Neo4j Context Engine Launches to Create AI Knowledge Layer and Enhance Agent Performance
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j announced the Neo4j Context Engine, a new product that lets enterprises rapidly build a shared knowledge layer — a reusable substrate that AI agents use to reason consistently over enterprise data. The engine includes a predefined six-layer business ontology, a graph-native memory layer for agent decision tracking, and simplified MCP server configuration for agent setup. It connects physical data sources directly to business logic so agents can make context-aware decisions without bespoke integration work per agent.
stories.why: This is exactly the architecture argument Graas makes: agents fail without a governed context layer underneath them. Neo4j shipping a named product with an ontology, memory, and MCP wiring gives sellers a credible anchor point when explaining why a knowledge graph is prerequisite infrastructure — and raises the competitive bar for any agent vendor that does not ship with one.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / build vs buy economics
stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 32% of Enterprises Skipped a Software Purchase to Build With Agentic Coding Tools
stories.body: McKinsey's August 25, 2026 State of AI survey (1,719 respondents across 97 countries) found that 32% of organizations decided against buying at least one software product or feature because they could build it in-house with agentic coding tools — rising to nearly half among AI high performers who attribute 5%+ of EBIT to AI. Large enterprises (over $1B revenue) scaling AI agents jumped from 27% to 40% year-over-year, while about one in five organizations report AI operating costs are already constraining AI use even as 60% plan to increase investment.
stories.why: This is the exact objection Graas sales teams face — 'we'll just build it.' McKinsey's data shows the build impulse is real but concentrated in a small high-performer cohort, while operating costs bite hardest among the builders themselves. Sellers can use the 20% cost-constraint finding and the flat EBIT impact figure (only 37% report any bottom-line effect) to reframe buy-vs-build conversations toward total cost of ownership.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / retail-CPG AI adoption
stories.title: Deloitte 2026 Retail & CPG Executive Survey: Enterprise-Wide AI Deployment Still in Single Digits Despite Broad Piloting
stories.body: Deloitte's 2026 State of AI in Retail and CPG survey of 200 executives found that enterprise-wide AI deployment sits at just 7–10% across both sectors — meaning the vast majority of investment remains in pilots. While 82% plan to increase AI budgets in the next 12 months, most incremental spend is going into IT and data infrastructure rather than value-generating use cases. On agentic commerce specifically, 40% of CPGs and 29% of retailers have no defined strategy yet, even as 50–60% are already piloting capabilities and prioritising API readiness.
stories.why: This is the pilot-stall story in hard numbers: single-digit enterprise deployment despite near-universal piloting is the exact problem Graas exists to solve. The finding that spend is pooling in infrastructure rather than outcomes gives sellers a credible framing for why customers need a proven deployment partner, not more internal experimentation budget.

stories.tag: US - agent vendor / Decagon product launch
stories.title: Decagon Launches Personal Agent Gateway and Four New Products at Dialogues 2026 to Handle AI-to-AI Support Calls
stories.body: At its October 1, 2026 Dialogues conference, Decagon shipped four products: Voice 3 (with a new duplex speech model called Chord), Personal Agent Gateway, Agent Modules, and Duet Apprentice. The Personal Agent Gateway detects when a customer's personal AI agent (such as Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, or Instinct) contacts support, routes it to a dedicated channel, and enforces scoped permissions the customer grants — accompanied by a new authorization protocol called PACT. Decagon also announced a Databricks partnership so its agents read real-time customer context directly from the lakehouse with no ETL, and joined the Databricks Marketplace.
stories.why: Decagon is a named competitor and the PACT protocol signals where the agent-to-agent commerce infrastructure race is heading: the retailer's AI concierge must be able to authenticate and serve a shopper's personal agent, not just a human. Graas sellers should understand this as a data-readiness story — the Databricks tie-in shows Decagon knows agents are only as good as the real-time context underneath them.

stories.tag: US - named CPG deployment / agent outcomes
stories.title: Tredence Agentic AI Recovers $6.5M in Trade Deductions for Enterprise CPG Client Across 30+ Systems
stories.body: Tredence published a documented deployment in which its agentic AI deduction-management solution, integrated across 30+ systems including SAP, EDI feeds, retailer portals, and email, automatically evaluated trade deductions, assigned reason codes, and recommended next-best actions for one enterprise CPG client. The result was $6.5M recovered from roughly $40M in addressable deduction spend. The case is part of a broader set of retail agent use cases published in October 2026 covering supply chain alert agents, dynamic pricing, and backend workflow automation.
stories.why: This is the proof-not-opinion story sellers need: a named CPG workflow (trade deduction resolution), a named multi-system integration challenge, and a hard dollar outcome ($6.5M on $40M addressable). It illustrates that agent value in retail/CPG is unlocked only when the agent has governed access to the right context across SAP, EDI, and retailer portals — precisely the data-foundation argument Graas makes.
